---
title: "Leagues & Clubs: Attacking Pace Across Europe"
toc: true
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Load dataset and compute individual season totals from per-90 rates
players <- read_delim(
  "2021-2022 Football Player Stats.csv",
  delim = ";",
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(Min)) |>
  mutate(
    Total_Goals = round(Goals * `90s`),
    Total_Assists = round(Assists * `90s`),
    Total_GC = Total_Goals + Total_Assists,
    Total_Shots = round(Shots * `90s`),
    Total_Press = Press * `90s`
  )

# Aggregate player stats up to the 98 clubs across the Big 5 leagues
# Bundesliga has 18 teams (34 matches); the other 4 leagues have 20 teams (38 matches)
clubs <- players |>
  summarize(
    Matches = if_else(first(Comp) == "Bundesliga", 34, 38),
    Squad_Goals = sum(Total_Goals, na.rm = TRUE),
    Squad_Assists = sum(Total_Assists, na.rm = TRUE),
    Squad_Shots = sum(Total_Shots, na.rm = TRUE),
    Goals_Per_Match = round(Squad_Goals / Matches, 2),
    Shots_Per_Match = round(Squad_Shots / Matches, 1),
    Press_Per_Match = round(sum(Total_Press, na.rm = TRUE) / Matches, 1),
    Scorers_5plus = sum(Total_Goals >= 5),
    Top_Player = Player[which.max(Total_GC)],
    Top_Player_Goals = Total_Goals[which.max(Total_GC)],
    Top_Player_GC = max(Total_GC),
    .by = c(Comp, Squad)
  )
```

Europe's "Big Five" domestic leagues share elite talent, yet they play noticeably different styles of football. Because the **Bundesliga** features 18 clubs playing **34 matches** each while the **Premier League**, **La Liga**, **Serie A**, and **Ligue 1** have 20 clubs playing **38 matches**, comparing raw season totals would undercount German clubs. Normalizing each squad's output on a **per-match** basis reveals how leagues and clubs truly separate.

## 1. Which League Plays the Most Open, High-Scoring Football?

Across all 98 clubs, the Bundesliga averaged **1.52 player-scored goals per team per match** (over 3.0 combined goals in a typical fixture), ahead of Serie A (1.38), the Premier League (1.36), and Ligue 1 (1.36). Spanish **La Liga** was Europe's tightest defensive competition at **1.22 goals per team per match**.

```{r}
p_league_dist <- clubs |>
  mutate(
    Comp = fct_reorder(Comp, Goals_Per_Match, .fun = median),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", Squad, "</b> (", Comp, ")<br>",
      "Goals per Match: <b>", Goals_Per_Match, "</b> (", Squad_Goals, " in ", Matches, " matches)<br>",
      "Shots per Match: ", Shots_Per_Match, "<br>",
      "Top Contributor: ", Top_Player, " (", Top_Player_GC, " G+A)"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Comp, y = Goals_Per_Match, color = Comp)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.38, alpha = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(aes(text = hover_text), width = 0.14, size = 2.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Club Scoring Rate Across Europe's Top Five Leagues (2021–2022)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Squad Goals Scored per Match"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p_league_dist, tooltip = "text", height = 430)
```

## 2. Pressing Intensity vs. Scoring Output Across All 98 Clubs

Do teams score more by pressing opponents high up the pitch, or by dominating possession? Plotting **presses per match** against **goals per match** highlights a striking tactical divide: possession powerhouses like **Manchester City** (2.53 goals/match, just 111.3 presses/match) rarely need to press because they keep the ball, whereas **Liverpool**, **Bayern Munich**, and **RB Leipzig** combine relentless pressing with elite scoring. Hover over any dot to inspect a club, or click league names in the legend to isolate specific competitions.

```{r}
p_club_style <- clubs |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", Squad, "</b> (", Comp, ")<br>",
      "Goals per Match: <b>", Goals_Per_Match, "</b> (", Squad_Goals, " total goals)<br>",
      "Presses per Match: ", Press_Per_Match, "<br>",
      "Players with 5+ Goals: ", Scorers_5plus, "<br>",
      "Top Star: ", Top_Player, " (", Top_Player_GC, " G+A)"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Press_Per_Match,
    y = Goals_Per_Match,
    color = Comp,
    size = Squad_Goals,
    text = hover_text
  )) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.78) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Club Pressing Intensity vs. Goals Scored per Match",
    x = "Team Defensive Presses per Match",
    y = "Team Goals Scored per Match",
    color = "League"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p_club_style, tooltip = "text", height = 500) |>
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.18))
```

## 3. Star Dependence vs. Shared Scoring Among Europe's Top 15 Attacks

Even among Europe's highest-scoring clubs, goals are distributed very differently. **Bayern Munich** (2.71 goals/match) and **Real Madrid** (2.11 goals/match) leaned heavily on Ballon d'Or contenders Robert Lewandowski (35 league goals) and Karim Benzema (27 league goals), whereas **Manchester City** won the Premier League with **eight different players scoring 5+ goals** and no single player exceeding 15.

```{r}
top15_long <- clubs |>
  slice_max(order_by = Goals_Per_Match, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    Rest_of_Squad_Goals = Squad_Goals - Top_Player_Goals,
    Squad_Label = fct_reorder(paste0(Squad, " (", Comp, ")"), Squad_Goals)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Top_Player_Goals, Rest_of_Squad_Goals),
    names_to = "Source",
    values_to = "Goals"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Source_Label = if_else(
      Source == "Top_Player_Goals",
      "Top Contributor's Goals",
      "Rest of Squad Goals"
    ),
    hover_text = if_else(
      Source == "Top_Player_Goals",
      paste0("<b>", Squad, "</b><br>Top Star: ", Top_Player, " (", Goals, " Goals, ", Top_Player_GC, " G+A)"),
      paste0("<b>", Squad, "</b><br>Rest of Squad: ", Goals, " Goals<br>Players with 5+ Goals: ", Scorers_5plus)
    )
  )

p_top15 <- ggplot(
  top15_long,
  aes(x = Goals, y = Squad_Label, fill = Source_Label, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Rest of Squad Goals" = "#6baed6",
    "Top Contributor's Goals" = "#d94801"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Season Goals Breakdown: Top Star vs. Rest of Squad (Top 15 Clubs)",
    x = "Total Player Goals in League Play (2021–2022)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggplotly(p_top15, tooltip = "text", height = 500) |>
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.16))
```
